author: SideCrab
name: SideCrab
description: An ambient Claude Code status panel for your iCUE display, with a pixel crab who reacts to what your sessions are doing. Live session cards with state, model and elapsed time; usage-limit gauges with reset countdowns, each one tappable for that window's detail â€” how full it is, when it resets, and when the recent burn rate would fill it; an alert when a session is waiting on you; today's token burn with a sparkline, an optional daily budget you can set, and today's cost when telemetry is on; a cross-session timeline and a seven-day strip you can tap into and page through a day at a time, plus a one-tap log of everything that happened today. Tap a waiting session to read its question and acknowledge it, tap the crab to acknowledge every waiting session at once, and pin the sessions you want kept at the front. When a session is waiting on a permission, approve or deny it right from the panel, with a countdown showing how long the decision can still be made there; on a working or finished session, tap to queue a next step, and the card shows what is queued until it runs. Filter the grid to the sessions waiting, working or finished, and switch between comfortable and compact cards to fit more of them on the glass. Each card carries a hairline showing how full that session's context window is, whenever its size is known. Quiet hours has a moon control beside the clock: tap for quiet for an hour, again to stay awake through tonight's window, again to hand it back to the schedule. Built for a fingertip: swipe a finished card away, press and hold a card to pin or unpin it, tap anywhere with two fingers to acknowledge everything at once, and pull down from the top edge to refresh now. The hardware row shows your CPU and GPU temperatures with the name of the sensor each reading comes from, so a mis-picked sensor is obvious at a glance, plus this PC's CPU and memory use while the companion is running - tap the row for the last ten minutes of both as a chart. Claude Code data needs the free SideCrab companion service running on the same PC, which the widget reads locally over http://127.0.0.1:2722 - see this listing for setup. Without it the panel still runs as a clock and CPU/GPU temperature display. It makes no other network requests, and sends nothing anywhere.
